SUBJECTIVE: 22-year-old female with known sickle cell disease (HbSS), diagnosed at age 2, presents to the emergency department with bilateral lower extremity pain that began approximately 6 hours ago. She describes the pain as deep, aching, and throbbing, rated 7 out of 10 in intensity. She reports taking ibuprofen 600 mg and acetaminophen 1000 mg at home without adequate relief. She also notes feeling warm and mildly fatigued. She denies cough, shortness of breath, chest pain, abdominal pain, headache, vision changes, or urinary symptoms. No recent travel or sick contacts. No history of DVT or pulmonary embolism.

OBJECTIVE: Temperature 38.3 degrees Celsius (101.0 degrees Fahrenheit), heart rate 98 bpm, blood pressure 112/68 mmHg, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, SpO2 98% on room air. General: Alert, oriented, appears uncomfortable but not in acute distress. HEENT: Scleral icterus noted bilaterally. Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, no wheezes, crackles, or rhonchi. Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, non-distended, no hepatosplenomegaly. Extremities: Bilateral tibial tenderness to palpation without swelling or erythema, no edema, no calf tenderness, no leg ulcers. Neurological: Alert and oriented x4, cranial nerves II-XII intact, no focal motor or sensory deficits, gait not assessed due to pain.

LABS: Hemoglobin 7.8 g/dL (baseline 8.2 g/dL), WBC 11.2 x 10^3/uL, platelets 289 x 10^3/uL, reticulocyte count 8.4%. Serum creatinine 0.7 mg/dL (baseline 0.6 mg/dL). LDH 342 U/L, total bilirubin 3.1 mg/dL. Blood cultures obtained. Chest X-ray: No acute cardiopulmonary disease, no infiltrates, no pleural effusions.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: (1) Acute sickle cell vaso-occlusive pain episode. Administered IV normal saline bolus 1 liter, IV morphine 4 mg with adequate pain relief achieved (pain reduced to 3/10). Patient monitored in ED for 4 hours with improvement. Not admitted. Discharged home with oral oxycodone 5 mg every 4-6 hours as needed for pain, ibuprofen 600 mg every 8 hours, and instructions to return if fever exceeds 38.5 degrees Celsius, or if she develops chest pain, shortness of breath, or worsening symptoms. Follow-up with hematology clinic in 48 hours. (2) Low-grade fever, temperature 38.3 degrees Celsius. Most likely related to vaso-occlusive crisis. Blood cultures pending. No signs of acute chest syndrome, sepsis, or other infectious source identified.

SUBJECTIVE: 17-year-old male with sickle cell disease (HbSS), on chronic transfusion program, presents with acute onset of severe generalized body pain rated 9 out of 10, productive cough with yellowish sputum, and progressive shortness of breath over the past 18 hours. He reports fever at home measured at 39.2 degrees Celsius (102.6 degrees Fahrenheit). He has had three prior hospitalizations for acute chest syndrome in the past two years. He denies headache, visual changes, abdominal pain, dysuria, or hematuria. No history of leg swelling, DVT, or pulmonary embolism. No depressive symptoms reported.

OBJECTIVE: Temperature 39.2 degrees Celsius (102.6 degrees Fahrenheit), heart rate 118 bpm, blood pressure 102/58 mmHg, respiratory rate 28 breaths/min, SpO2 88% on room air. General: Acutely ill-appearing, diaphoretic, using accessory muscles of respiration. HEENT: Scleral icterus, dry mucous membranes. Lungs: Decreased breath sounds at right lower lobe with dullness to percussion and bronchial breath sounds; scattered crackles bilaterally. Cardiovascular: Tachycardic, regular rhythm, grade II/VI systolic flow murmur at left sternal border. Abdomen: Mild splenomegaly palpated 2 cm below left costal margin, no acute tenderness. Extremities: Diffuse tenderness in bilateral upper and lower extremities, no edema, no calf tenderness, no leg ulcers. Neurological: Alert and oriented x3, no focal neurological deficits, moving all extremities symmetrically, cranial nerves intact.

LABS: Hemoglobin 6.2 g/dL (baseline 9.0 g/dL), WBC 18.7 x 10^3/uL with 8% bands, platelets 198 x 10^3/uL, reticulocyte count 12.1%. HbS level 78%. Serum creatinine 0.9 mg/dL (baseline 0.8 mg/dL, ratio 1.13x baseline). LDH 687 U/L, total bilirubin 5.8 mg/dL, AST 62 U/L, ALT 38 U/L. ABG: pH 7.38, PaCO2 32 mmHg, PaO2 58 mmHg on room air. Blood cultures obtained; pending at time of admission. Chest X-ray: New right lower lobe consolidation with air bronchograms consistent with a new lobar infiltrate. No pleural effusion. CT pulmonary angiography: No evidence of pulmonary embolism; confirmed right lower lobe consolidation.

HOSPITAL COURSE: Patient admitted to the medical floor. Initiated on ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily and azithromycin 500 mg IV for empiric coverage of acute chest syndrome. IV morphine PCA established for pain management. Initially placed on supplemental oxygen via nasal cannula at 4 L/min (FiO2 approximately 36%), achieving SpO2 of 92%. On hospital day 2, respiratory status worsened with increasing tachypnea (RR 34) and SpO2 dropping to 84% on nasal cannula. Transitioned to high-flow nasal cannula at 40 L/min with FiO2 60%, achieving SpO2 of 93%. Patient did not require intubation, vasopressors, or other life-support interventions. Hematology consulted and recommended urgent exchange transfusion due to progressive acute chest syndrome. Automated red cell exchange performed, reducing HbS from 78% to 28%, with post-procedure hemoglobin of 10.1 g/dL. Patient demonstrated significant clinical improvement over the following 48 hours. Weaned to low-flow nasal cannula by day 4 and to room air by day 5. Pain gradually improved and PCA discontinued on day 4, transitioned to oral analgesics.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY: Temperature normalized by hospital day 3. Blood cultures returned negative. Repeat chest X-ray showed improving right lower lobe infiltrate. Serum creatinine remained stable at 0.9 mg/dL throughout admission. No evidence of DVT on bilateral lower extremity Doppler ultrasound. No neurological complications observed. No arrhythmias noted on telemetry monitoring. Discharged on hospital day 7 in stable condition with follow-up in sickle cell clinic in one week.

DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES: (1) Acute chest syndrome, severe, requiring high-flow oxygen therapy and exchange transfusion. (2) Acute sickle cell vaso-occlusive pain crisis complicated by acute chest syndrome. (3) Fever secondary to acute chest syndrome.

SUBJECTIVE: 29-year-old male with sickle cell disease (HbSC), known history of avascular necrosis of the right hip (managed conservatively), presents via EMS to the emergency department with acute severe chest pain, progressive dyspnea, and high-grade fever for the past 8 hours. His wife reports he had been experiencing a vaso-occlusive pain crisis at home for two days managed with oral hydromorphone, but acutely worsened with onset of chest pain and difficulty breathing. She notes he became confused and less responsive during transport. No prior history of stroke, DVT, or PE. No psychiatric history or depressive symptoms.

OBJECTIVE: Temperature 39.8 degrees Celsius (103.6 degrees Fahrenheit), heart rate 132 bpm, blood pressure 78/42 mmHg, respiratory rate 36 breaths/min, SpO2 79% on 15 L non-rebreather mask. General: Critically ill-appearing, obtunded, diaphoretic, severe respiratory distress with use of accessory muscles, intercostal and suprasternal retractions. HEENT: Scleral icterus, dry mucous membranes. Lungs: Diffuse bilateral crackles with diminished breath sounds in bilateral lower lobes. Cardiovascular: Tachycardic, distant heart sounds, no appreciable murmur. Abdomen: Distended, diffusely tender, hepatomegaly palpated 4 cm below right costal margin. Extremities: Cool, mottled, capillary refill greater than 4 seconds bilaterally, no peripheral edema, no leg ulcers. Neurological: GCS 10 (E2 V3 M5), pupils 3 mm bilaterally and reactive, withdraws to pain in all extremities. No lateralizing signs.

LABS: Hemoglobin 5.1 g/dL (baseline 11.5 g/dL), WBC 24.3 x 10^3/uL with 15% bands, platelets 89 x 10^3/uL, reticulocyte count 14.2%. HbS level 52%. Serum creatinine 2.4 mg/dL (baseline 1.0 mg/dL, 2.4x baseline). BUN 38 mg/dL. LDH 1247 U/L, total bilirubin 9.6 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 4.2 mg/dL, AST 189 U/L, ALT 94 U/L. Lactate 6.8 mmol/L. Procalcitonin 8.4 ng/mL. ABG: pH 7.22, PaCO2 28 mmHg, PaO2 48 mmHg on 15 L NRB. Coagulation: INR 1.8, aPTT 42 seconds. Blood cultures: Two sets drawn from peripheral sites. Chest X-ray: Bilateral diffuse alveolar infiltrates with consolidation in all lobes, small bilateral pleural effusions. CT pulmonary angiography: No evidence of pulmonary embolism; confirmed bilateral multilobar consolidations consistent with acute chest syndrome. Lower extremity Doppler ultrasound: No evidence of deep vein thrombosis. Urine output: 15 mL in the first 2 hours (oliguria).

ICU COURSE: Patient emergently intubated in the ED for acute hypoxemic respiratory failure with deteriorating mental status (GCS 10). Post-intubation ventilator settings: assist-control mode, FiO2 100%, PEEP 10 cmH2O, tidal volume 400 mL (6 mL/kg IBW). Aggressive fluid resuscitation initiated with 30 mL/kg crystalloid bolus. Despite 2 liters of IV normal saline, blood pressure remained 72/38 mmHg with MAP 49. Central venous catheter placed in the right internal jugular vein and norepinephrine infusion started at 0.15 mcg/kg/min, titrated to 0.3 mcg/kg/min to achieve MAP greater than 65 mmHg. Vasopressin 0.04 units/min added as a second vasopressor. Broad-spectrum antibiotics initiated: vancomycin 1.5 g IV, meropenem 1 g IV every 8 hours, and azithromycin 500 mg IV daily. Urgent automated red cell exchange transfusion performed, reducing HbS from 52% to 18%, with post-exchange hemoglobin of 9.8 g/dL.

On ICU day 2, blood cultures returned positive for Streptococcus pneumoniae in both sets; antibiotics narrowed to ceftriaxone based on susceptibilities. Repeat ABG showed improvement: pH 7.31, PaCO2 34 mmHg, PaO2 72 mmHg on FiO2 80%. Serum creatinine peaked at 2.8 mg/dL on day 2 (2.8 times baseline of 1.0 mg/dL). Urine output improved to 0.5 mL/kg/hr after hemodynamic stabilization; renal replacement therapy was not required. By ICU day 4, vasopressors successfully weaned off and FiO2 reduced to 50%. Extubated on ICU day 6 to high-flow nasal cannula, then weaned to room air by day 8. Transferred to medical floor on day 7. Mental status returned to baseline. No seizures or focal neurological deficits observed throughout admission. No arrhythmias on continuous telemetry.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY: Creatinine normalized to 1.1 mg/dL by discharge. Repeat chest X-ray showed near-complete resolution of bilateral infiltrates. No evidence of pulmonary embolism, stroke, or other neurological complications. Hearing intact bilaterally. PHQ-9 score 3 (minimal depression). Patient discharged on hospital day 14 in stable condition with close hematology follow-up.

DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES: (1) Acute chest syndrome, life-threatening, requiring invasive mechanical ventilation and vasopressor support. (2) Acute sickle cell vaso-occlusive crisis complicated by acute chest syndrome and requiring life-supporting interventions. (3) Sepsis secondary to Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteremia with septic shock requiring vasopressor therapy. (4) Acute kidney injury, KDIGO stage 2, creatinine 2.8 times baseline, resolved without dialysis. (5) Fever, temperature 39.8 degrees Celsius.
